articles.title: Why an Optimizer?
articles.excerpt: Using an optimizer will give you better results than the traditional approach. See why.
articles.html:
Why We Use the Heuristic Approach with Optimization

Before you dive into scheduling, it’s worth understanding why XO combines heuristics with optimization. This short video walks you through a simple example showing how traditional, one-class-at-a-time scheduling can lead to bottlenecks — and how XO’s combined approach plans ahead, matches resources smarter, maximizes results, and boosts your overall profit.

We hope this made everything clear—and turned you into a fan of our optimizer, just like us!

articles.title: 🧰 New Resource – How to Add a New Resource (Overview)
articles.excerpt: How to add a new resource in XO Scheduler, using an Instructor as an example.
articles.html:
🌟 Your training organization relies on many types of resources—classrooms, simulators, instructors, and more. In XO Scheduler, you can add and manage these resources in just a few clicks.

This article will walk you through adding a new resource step by step, using an Instructor as our example and links to detailed guides for each resource type.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Adding a New Resource

Watch this quick video to see exactly how to add a New Resource Instructor in XO Scheduler.

📌 Disclaimer: Screenshots and videos may look slightly different from your XO Scheduler interface depending on your version or configuration.

🧩 Resource Types You Can Add

In XO Scheduler, you can create and manage Instructors, Simulators, Classrooms, and other resources that you need in your company.

📌 Wrapping Up

This overview is your first step toward organizing your operation in XO Scheduler. Start with the resource type that matters most, then continue adding the rest to keep your scheduling accurate and efficient.

articles.title: 👨‍🏫 New Resource – Instructor
articles.excerpt: How to add a New Resource "Instructor" into the XO System
articles.html:
🌟 Instructors are one of the most important resources in your training organization. When you add a new Instructor in XO Scheduler, you’re not just creating a name in the system—you’re defining key details that affect scheduling accuracy: qualifications, costs, work rules (to ensure legal rest times and proper scheduling), etc.

This article shows you step-by-step how to add a new Instructor resource. For bulk creation, see: How to Import Resources from Excel.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Adding a New Instructor

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

1) Start the Process — Right-click in the Resource area and select Create Resource.

2) Choose the Resource Type — From the list of resource types, select Instructor. You can manage or add new resource types in another tutorial.

3) Open the Resource Form — Click to open the input form for the selected resource type.

4) Understand Field Requirements — Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are mandatory. Typical mandatory fields: ID (must be unique), First Name, Last Name, Location, Cost per Hour.

5) Upload a Photo — Upload a profile picture for the instructor (optional but recommended).

6) Fill in Resource Details — Complete all required and relevant information.

7) Assign Work Rules (or Time Slots) — Assign Work Rules (e.g., London Work Rules) to ensure instructors' hours and rest times are respected by the system. Important: a resource can have either Work Rules or Time Slots, but not both.

8) Save the Resource — Click Save. The new Instructor will appear at the top of the resource list, regardless of filters.

💡 Pro Tips

Work Rules are critical: without them, XO Scheduler won't enforce proper rest or maximum working hours. Qualify your resources: assign qualifications to each instructor—without them, the system won't schedule that resource. Use Excel import for bulk setup: save time if you have many instructors to add.

Wrapping Up

Adding instructors is more than just entering names into XO Scheduler—it's about setting them up for accurate, compliant scheduling. Assign Work Rules so the system respects rest times and maximum working hours, and add all relevant Qualifications, or the system won't schedule that instructor at all. Once your instructors are properly configured, scheduling becomes smoother, safer, and far more efficient.

articles.title: 📥 Import Resources to XO
articles.excerpt: How to Import Resources from an excel sheet into the XO System
articles.html:
🌟 If you’re setting up XO Scheduler for the first time or updating your organization with many new team members, Excel Import is the fastest way to add resources.

Instead of creating each Instructor, Classroom, or Simulator manually, you can upload them in bulk directly from your existing spreadsheets. This guide shows you exactly how to import your resources step by step, and how to ensure they’re properly configured (with Qualifications and Work Rules) after import so scheduling is accurate.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Importing Resources

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide (example: importing a spreadsheet of Instructors)

1) Start the Import Process — Right-click in the Resources area and select Import Resources.

2) Select Your Excel File — Choose the Excel file you want to import (example: updated_instructors.xlsx).

3) Confirm Header Row — Indicate if your Excel file has a header row (column names), e.g. first row contains "ID", "First Name", "Last Name", etc.

4) Map Excel Columns to Resource Properties — XO Scheduler will try to auto-map columns based on names; review and adjust as needed (e.g., if your column says "Rules" but XO expects "Work Rules", map it manually). Common properties to map: Type, ID, First Name, Last Name, Location, Department, Work Rules or Time Slots.

5) Start the Import — Click Import and confirm the success message (e.g., "200 resources imported").

6) Organize Imported Resources — For easier organization, assign all imported entries to a temporary department in Excel, such as "Imported Employees". After importing, filter by this department and move resources to their correct departments.

Example Workflow Summary: Excel file → updated_instructors.xlsx | Header row → Yes | Column mapping → adjust Rules to Work Rules | Department (in Excel) → Imported Employees | Post-import task → reassign to correct departments.

💡 Pro Tips

Qualify your resources immediately: once imported, assign Qualifications (licenses, language skills, visas, etc.) — without these, XO Scheduler won't schedule them. Set Work Rules to ensure correct rest times and hour limits. Keep Excel clean: check for duplicate IDs or missing required fields before importing. Use departments strategically: import everything into a "Staging" department, then reorganize.

Wrapping Up

Excel Import is a powerful way to onboard your team quickly, saving hours of manual data entry. But importing is only the first step—make sure every resource is qualified and has the right Work Rules to ensure accurate, compliant scheduling.

articles.title: 📜 Work Rules – Define Duty Limits and Rest Periods
articles.excerpt: Understand and Manage Work Rules for Instructors
articles.html:
🌟 Work Rules are essential for safe, compliant scheduling. They define the limits for your instructors’ and other human resources’ duty periods, working hours, and required rest times. Without Work Rules, your organization risks regulatory issues.

This guide is divided into two parts: Understanding Work Rules (what they are and why they matter), and Managing Work Rules (how to create and assign them in XO Scheduler).

🎥 Video Tutorial: Work Rules Explained

🧩 Part 1: Understanding Work Rules

Work Rules in XO Scheduler define when and how people can be scheduled. They ensure legal, contractual, and safety requirements are followed—especially important in 24/7 training operations.

Key Terms: Max Work Time (continuous working time without a break, e.g. maximum 6 hours in the simulator); Max Duty Time (total time between the first and last task of a shift, including breaks — e.g. briefing at 21:00, debriefing at 6:00 = 9 hours duty); Min Rest Time Between Duties (minimum rest before the next shift starts); Days Off (required rest days in a rolling work window, e.g. 2 days off every 7 days).

Real-World Examples

🧑‍💼 Office Worker Example — works 09:00–13:00 and 14:00–18:00. Max Work Time: 4 hours. Max Duty Time: 9 hours (09:00–18:00). Days Off: weekends.

🧑‍✈️ Flight Instructor Example — briefing at 21:00, simulator session, then debrief at 06:00. Max Work Time: 6 hours (active sim + briefings). Max Duty Time: 9 hours (entire span). Min Rest Time: 12 hours before next duty (cannot start before 18:00).

📌 Key Distinction: Duty Time refers to the full duration from the first task assigned (e.g., briefing at 21:00) to the final task (e.g., debriefing at 6:00). Even if breaks occur during this window, the entire period counts. Work Time, by contrast, only includes active working periods like the simulator session.

Days Off Rules: XO Scheduler allows you to specify required days off in a rolling window (e.g., 2 in every 7 days), and whether those days off must be consecutive.

🛠️ Part 2: Managing Work Rules in XO Scheduler

Below is a step-by-step guide to create, configure, and assign Work Rules within the XO System.

Step-by-Step: Creating a Work Rule

1) Go to Time Slots and Work Rules.

2) Scroll to the bottom → Right-click → Create Work Rule.

3) Name the rule (e.g., London Work Rules).

4) Enter time values (in minutes) according to your policies: Max Work Time = 360 (6 hours), Max Duty Time = 540 (9 hours), Min Rest Time = 720 (12 hours), Days Off Rule = 2 days off in 7 days (toggle consecutive if needed).

5) Click Save.

Step-by-Step: Assigning Work Rules

1) Open the Resources section.

2) Select the resource(s) (e.g., Instructors).

3) Click Edit Resource.

4) Choose a Work Rule from the dropdown menu.

5) Click Save.

💡 You can show the Work Rule column in your resource table by right-clicking column headers and enabling it.

💡 Pro Tips

Always assign Work Rules: without them, the system won't respect rules or maximum working hours. Use clear naming conventions: if you have different bases or regions, name rules like "London Work Rules", "NYC Rules". Review regularly: regulations and company policies change—keep your Work Rules updated.

Wrapping Up

Work Rules are the foundation for safe and accurate scheduling in XO Scheduler. By setting clear duty limits, rest requirements, and days off, you're protecting your team, staying compliant, and ensuring training quality. Once you've created and assigned Work Rules, combine them with Qualifications to get a scheduling system that is both powerful and realistic.

articles.title: 🏫 New Resource – Classroom
articles.excerpt: How to add a New Resource "classroom" into the XO System
articles.html:
In this guide, you’ll learn how to add a new classroom as a resource into the XO system.

🌟 Classrooms are essential training resources for briefings, debriefings, and ground training. Adding them correctly ensures the system can schedule them reliably.

The process is very similar to adding an Instructor, so if you haven’t yet, we recommend reviewing New Resource – Instructor first. This guide focuses on the specific fields and steps unique to Classrooms.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

1) Start the creation process — Right-click in the Resources area and select Create Resource.

2) Choose the resource type — From the list, select Classroom. (You can manage or create new resource types if needed, see Manage Properties.)

3) Open the resource form — Click to open the Classroom resource input form.

4) Fill in resource details — Mandatory fields (marked with *) usually include ID (must be unique), Name, Location, Cost per Hour.

💰 A Note About Costs: the Cost per Hour field helps the system calculate and compare resources when optimizing schedules. If unsure, use a standard placeholder (e.g., 100) to give the system a baseline — you can always adjust this value later.

5) Leave Time Slots and Work Rules empty — Classrooms do not require Time Slots or Work Rules. Leaving these blank means classrooms are available 24/7 unless restricted by location or qualifications.

6) Save the resource — Click Save. The new Classroom appears at the top of the list, regardless of filters.

✅ Important: after creating the Classroom, assign it a Qualification (e.g., General Classroom) so XO Scheduler can automatically allocate it to training events.

💡 Pro Tips

Be consistent with IDs and names: use a naming scheme like CR-001, Briefing Room 1. Set Costs early: even if approximate, it improves scheduling efficiency. Always qualify classrooms: without qualifications, they won't be scheduled.

📌 Wrapping Up

Adding a Classroom is simple and similar to adding an Instructor, with the key differences being no Time Slots or Work Rules. Once created, don't forget to assign Qualifications so they can be scheduled correctly. Next, continue by setting up your Simulators or use Excel Import if you need to onboard multiple resources at once.

articles.title: 🕹 New Resource – Simulator
articles.excerpt: How to add a New Resource "Simulator" into the XO system
articles.html:
🌟 Simulators are high-value resources that drive your training throughput and costs. Adding them correctly—especially setting Time Slots and core details—ensures XO Scheduler can allocate them efficiently and profitably.

This article walks you through creating a Simulator resource, step by step, with annotated screenshots. If you're already familiar with adding Instructors, this process will feel very similar.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

1) Start the creation process — Right-click in the Resources area and select Create Resource.

2) Choose the resource type — From the list of available types, select Simulator.

3) Open the resource editor — Click to open the input form for the Simulator resource.

4) Understand field requirements — Mandatory fields (marked with *) typically include ID (must be unique), Name, Location, Cost per Hour, Time Slots.

5) Fill in Resource Details — example entries: ID = SIM-A320-01 (must be unique within the system), Name = A320 Full Flight Sim (simulator's display name), Location = Singapore (used for location-based scheduling), Cost per Hour = 100 (mandatory, used by the cost optimizer). Replace these with details specific to your own simulator.

6) Assign Time Slots — Simulators typically operate within defined Time Slots (e.g., morning, evening). Select a Time Slot set from the dropdown (created by an admin). Without Time Slots, XO may treat the simulator as unavailable. Choose Time Slots OR Work Rules — never both.

7) Leave Work Rules empty — Simulators are non-human resources, so Work Rules do not apply.

8) Save the resource — Click Save. The new Simulator appears at the top of your list.

Important: don't forget to qualify your simulators (e.g., “A320 Certified Device”) so XO can assign them automatically.

💡 Pro Tips

Set Time Slots first: clarifies when simulators are available. Check IDs and names: use a clear, consistent naming convention. Qualify simulators: without qualifications, they won't be scheduled.

📌 Wrapping Up

Adding a Simulator is simple when you know which details matter most: Time slots, qualifications, and consistent identifiers. Once your simulators are set up, continue by adding other critical resources like Classrooms and Instructors.

articles.title: 🎓 Qualify Resources
articles.excerpt: Learn how to qualify your resources in the XO System
articles.html:
Qualifying your resources (like instructors, classrooms, and simulators) ensures the XO Scheduler can automatically assign them to appropriate training events. This guide explains how to assign qualifications to your resource step by step.

Example Scenario: you're planning a Human Factors training session in the United States, which involves a classroom, several trainees, and an instructor. To ensure proper scheduling, you need to qualify the instructor with relevant certifications (e.g., Human Factors, English, and US Visa), and the classroom with a general classroom qualification, because in this example the classroom doesn't need special qualifications/requirements.

We highly recommend you watch the video. It explains why Qualifications are important and then shows you a step by step guide.

  1. Instructor Qualification

To make sure instructors are eligible for automatic assignment, they must hold the appropriate qualifications — such as the topic of the training, language skills, or travel visas.

Here's how to qualify an instructor: search for the instructor by name; double-click to open their profile → go to the Records tab; review existing qualifications (e.g., English C1). To add a new qualification (e.g., US Visa): right-click → Create Record, search for the qualification, select it, set Issuing Country (e.g. USA) and Expiration Date (e.g. July 30, 2028) — please enter the details according to your specific company's needs — then click Save.

📝 The system will not auto-assign instructors to events beyond the qualification's expiration date.

  1. Classroom Qualification

Even if the resource is named "General Classroom," you still need to formally qualify it. This lets the system recognize it as an eligible space for training.

To assign a qualification to a classroom: open the classroom's profile by double-clicking on its name in the resource section; go to the Records tab; right-click → Create Record; search for "General Classroom Qualification"; select it; leave the expiration blank (for unlimited validity); click Save.

📌 Classrooms must be qualified to be included in automatic scheduling.

  1. Simulator Qualification

Simulators must be qualified based on the aircraft type or training device configuration they support.

To qualify a simulator: search for the simulator you want to qualify; open its profile by double-clicking on its name in the resource section; go to the Records tab; right-click → Create Record; search "A320 Certified Device"; select it; enter the issue date and, if applicable, an expiration date (both are optional). Your window may look slightly different depending on your company's configuration — additional optional fields may appear (for example, Comment or Deactivated Yes/No); fill in what's relevant for your organization. Click Save.

⚙️ Without qualification, the simulator will not appear in assignment suggestions.

Result

You now have a qualified instructor, a classroom, and a simulator.

articles.title: 📑 Qualify Resources: Managing Documents
articles.excerpt: Learn how to create and manage Documents (qualifications) in XO Scheduler
articles.html:
🌟 In XO Scheduler, qualifications are stored as Documents. Every Instructor, Classroom, Simulator, and other resource must have at least one valid qualification (document) for the system to schedule them.

Documents are individual qualifications, while Document Types are templates that define what fields each qualification should have. This guide walks you through creating and deleting Documents, creating and managing Document Types, and understanding how qualifications tie directly to scheduling.

Without these documents, your resources will not appear as assignable in schedules.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

📄 How to Create a Document

1) Go to Setup → Documents.

2) Right-click in the document list.

3) Select Create Document and choose a Document Type.

4) Fill in the required fields (e.g., document name, issue date, expiry date).

5) Click Save.

🗑️ How to Delete a Document

1) Go to Setup → Documents.

2) Right-click the document you want to delete.

3) Select Delete Document…

4) Confirm deletion.

🏷️ How to Create a Document Type

Document Types are templates for qualifications, defining which fields each document will contain.

1) Go to Setup → Properties.

2) Select Manage properties for: Records.

3) In the Document Types list, right-click and choose Create Document Type…

4) Enter a name for the new type (e.g., Type Rating – A320).

5) Click Save.

💡 Pro Tips

Qualifications = Documents: a resource cannot be scheduled without at least one valid document. Use expiry dates: adding expiration fields prevents scheduling unqualified instructors or equipment. Plan your Document Types early: create templates for your most common records first (licenses, approvals, device certifications). Keep documents organized: use clear names like "A320 Type Rating" or "Simulator Certified".

articles.title: 📘 Create a Curriculum – Overview
articles.excerpt: Learn how to create and manage curriculums in XO Scheduler in this four-part series.
articles.html:
🌟 A curriculum is the foundation of all scheduled classes in XO Scheduler. Every training session must be based on a curriculum, which defines the training days, topics, required qualifications, and scheduling rules.

This series of articles will guide you through the full process of building a curriculum, from creating the layout to enforcing continuity rules.

🎥 Curriculum Video Playlist — this playlist contains all 4 curriculum tutorials so you can follow the entire process step by step: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLg9yN9vF9j7Uc3bO7C-e1DssKT8QkYQAH

🧩 The Four Parts of Curriculum Creation

Part 1 – Building the Layout: learn how to create the structure of your curriculum, including training days, topics, and scheduling strategies.

Part 2 – Assigning Qualifications: see how to add resource slots so XO Scheduler only assigns qualified instructors, simulators, and classrooms.

Part 3 – Joining Crews: discover how to combine multiple crews into shared sessions, such as Human Factors or Ground School.

Part 4 – Continuity: apply continuity rules that ensure resources stay consistent—or intentionally change—across related training sessions.

💡 Pro Tips

Build step by step: don't skip ahead—each part builds on the previous one. Use qualifications consistently: without them, XO Scheduler cannot assign resources. Balance realism and flexibility: continuity rules should reflect your actual training policies.

📌 Wrapping Up

Creating a curriculum may seem complex at first, but XO Scheduler breaks it down into clear steps. By following this series, you'll design curriculums that are flexible, compliant, and easy to reuse across your training operation. Start with Part 1 – Building the Layout to begin your curriculum setup.

articles.title: 📕 Create a Curriculum – Part 1: Building the Layout
articles.excerpt: Learn how to create the structure of a curriculum in XO Scheduler, including days, topics, and scheduling strategies.
articles.html:
🌟 A curriculum is the foundation of every training class in XO Scheduler. Without a curriculum, you cannot plan or schedule any sessions. In this first part of our series, we'll walk through building a curriculum layout, including day types, topics, and strategies for automatic scheduling.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Curriculum Layout — this video shows how to build a new curriculum layout step by step.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

We'll use a B747 Three-Day Recurrent Training as our example (like in the video).

1) Create a new curriculum — Go to the Curriculum page; right-click → Create Curriculum; fill in properties (use presets if available). Example: Name → B747 Three-Day Recurrent, Training Type → Recurrent.

2) Define training days:

Day 1: Fixed start times. Add topic: Human Factors, 08:00–12:00 (240 minutes). Add topic: Ground School, 14:00–16:00 (120 minutes).

Day 2: Flexible start times. Add topics: Briefing (90 min), Simulator (240 min), Debriefing (60 min). Give the simulator a distinct color in the Gantt chart.

Day 3: Duplicate Day 2, then rename it.

3) Set Turn Time and Next Training Day — Turn Time: minimum rest between training days (e.g., 720 minutes = 12 hours). Next Training Day: define required breaks (e.g., min 1 day, max 3 days).

4) Save the curriculum — Click Save to store your layout.

💡 Pro Tips

Use presets: save time by reusing standard property values. Color-code topics: helps visualize training days on the Gantt chart. Always define Turn Time: prevents back-to-back scheduling that ignores rest.

📌 Wrapping Up

You've now built the structure of a curriculum with days and topics. Next, we'll show you how to link these topics with qualifications so XO Scheduler can assign the right resources automatically.

articles.title: 📗 Create a Curriculum – Part 2: Assigning Qualifications
articles.excerpt: Learn how to assign qualifications to topics using resource slots in XO Scheduler.
articles.html:
🌟 Curriculums don't reference specific instructors or devices. Instead, they use resource slots that are defined by qualifications. This allows XO Scheduler to assign the right qualified resource automatically when building schedules.

In this part, we'll add qualifications to our B747 recurrent curriculum.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Assigning Qualifications — this video shows how to use resource slots to link topics with required qualifications.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

We'll focus on Day 2 and Day 3 of the B747 recurrent training.

1) Create a simulator slot — Go to the Resource Slots page. Create → Name: Simulator. Role: Device. Qualification: B747 Level C Simulator. Restrict Location: Yes. Assignment Policy: Less fragmented.

2) Create an instructor slot — Create → Name: Sim Instructor. Role: Instructor. Qualification: B747 Sim Instructor. Restrict Location: No. Assignment Policy: Balanced.

3) Assign slots to topics — Assign Simulator slot → Sim 1 + Sim 2. Assign Sim Instructor slot → Briefing, Sim, and Debriefing on Days 2 & 3.

💡 Pro Tips

Use roles correctly: Device vs Instructor vs Classroom. Balance policies wisely: Balanced for people, Less Fragmented for devices. Check location restrictions: simulators usually cannot travel, but instructors can.

📌 Wrapping Up

Your curriculum topics now have resource slots linked to qualifications. XO Scheduler can now assign only qualified instructors and simulators. Next, we'll show you how to join multiple crews into a shared session when needed.

articles.title: 📙 Create a Curriculum – Part 3: Joining Crews
articles.excerpt: Learn how to use the join function in XO Scheduler to combine multiple crews into one shared class.
articles.html:
🌟 Sometimes, multiple crews start training together before splitting into individual simulator sessions. XO Scheduler supports this with the join function, which lets you assign one classroom and instructor across several crews.

In this part, we'll show how to create joinable slots for Human Factors and Ground School in the B747 recurrent curriculum.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Joining Crews — this video explains how to set up joinable resource slots and content IDs.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

1) Create resource slots for Day 1:

Human Factors Facility: Role = Classroom, Qualification = Human Factors Classroom, Assignment = Less Fragmented.

Human Factors Instructor: Role = Instructor, Qualification = Human Factors Instructor, Assignment = Balanced.

Ground School Facility: Role = Classroom, Qualification = B747 Ground School Classroom, Assignment = Less Fragmented.

Ground School Instructor: Role = Instructor, Qualification = B747 Ground School Instructor, Assignment = Balanced.

2) Assign slots to topics — Assign Human Factors slots to the Human Factors topic. Assign Ground School slots to the Ground School topic.

3) Set joinable properties — For each slot, double-click and mark it as Joinable. Enter a Content ID (e.g., HF-Instructor, B747-GS-Facility). Topics with the same Content ID can be joined, even across different fleets.

💡 Pro Tips

Content IDs are critical: define a company policy for consistent IDs. Check qualified resources: always verify the resource list is not empty. Fleet vs non-fleet topics: Human Factors can be joined across fleets; fleet-specific ground schools cannot.

📌 Wrapping Up

You've now set up joinable topics so multiple crews can train together when needed. Next, we'll add continuity rules to ensure resources (like instructors) stay consistent across related sessions.

articles.title: 📒 Create a Curriculum – Part 4: Continuity Rules
articles.excerpt: Learn how to apply continuity rules in XO Scheduler to keep (or separate) resources across multiple topics.
articles.html:
🌟 Continuity defines whether the same resource should be used across related training slots. XO Scheduler supports three types:

Required Continuity → must be the same resource (e.g., same instructor for briefing, sim, debriefing).

Preferred Continuity → use the same resource if possible (e.g., same simulator across days).

Discontinuity → must be a different resource (e.g., different instructor for LOE vs simulator sessions).

🎥 Video Tutorial: Continuity Rules — this video demonstrates how to set Required, Preferred, and Discontinuity rules.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

1) Required Continuity — Right-click Day 2 → Create Continuity → Sim Instructor. Name: Day2 Sim Instructor. Repeat for Day 3.

2) Preferred Continuity — Click Create. Filter by Role = Device. Select Simulators for Day 2 & Day 3. Set type = Preferred. Name: Sim Day2-3.

3) Discontinuity — Duplicate Day 3 to create Day 4 (LOE). Rename topics and assign new color. Create continuity → filter by Instructor. Mark Day 2 & Day 3 instructors with "D". Right-click Day 4 instructor slot, mark as Discontinuity. Name: LOE Discontinuity.

💡 Pro Tips

Use meaningful names: helps quickly identify continuity rules later. Check assignments visually: select a slot to highlight all assigned topics. Balance realism and flexibility: use required only when necessary; preferred keeps scheduling efficient.

📌 Wrapping Up

Continuity rules give you control over how resources are reused across sessions. With required, preferred, and discontinuity settings, you can balance consistency and flexibility in your schedules. Now that your curriculum is complete, you're ready to integrate it into your training plans and let XO Scheduler optimize sessions automatically.

articles.title: 🎰 Time Slots – Organizing Simulator Availability
articles.excerpt: Learn how to create and manage Time Slots in XO Scheduler to organize simulator availability for flexible scheduling.
articles.html:
🌟 Time Slots are a simple but powerful way to control when simulator sessions can start. Instead of fixing start times in your curriculum, XO Scheduler uses Time Slots to decide which simulator blocks are available. This gives the Optimizer flexibility to find the best start times based on real resource availability.

🎥 Video Tutorial: Time Slots (former Sim Slots) — this video walks you through creating Time Slots and assigning preferences step by step.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

We'll use creating five 4-hour slots as our example.

1) Open the Time Slots page — Go to the Time Slots page in XO Scheduler. Right-click in the Time Slots area. Choose Create Time Slots.

2) Name and create the slots group — Give the group a name, e.g., "5 Slots". Click the plus (+) button for each slot you want to add.

3) Define slot start times and durations:

Slot 1: Start 07:00 AM, Duration 240 min (4 hrs).

Slot 2: Start 11:00 AM, Duration 240 min.

Slot 3: Start 03:00 PM, Duration 240 min.

Slot 4: Start 07:00 PM, Duration 240 min.

Slot 5: Start 11:00 PM, Duration 240 min.

4) Set reward factors (optional) — Use Reward Factor to make certain slots preferred. Example: 11:00 slot → 1.1 (10% more desirable). Example: 15:00 slot → 1.05 (5% more desirable). Slots with equal factors are treated equally by the optimizer.

5) Save and assign to simulators — Click Save. The new Time Slots group can now be assigned to any simulator resource.

💡 Pro Tips

Use reward factors strategically: make peak or highly efficient slots slightly more attractive. Standardize slot groups: consistent naming (e.g., Standard-5x4h) makes assigning to simulators faster. Match operational hours: align slot start times with your facility's open hours or staffing patterns. Review assignments: always confirm simulators are assigned to a slot group; otherwise, they may appear unavailable.

📌 Wrapping Up

Time Slots give you fine control over simulator availability while keeping schedules flexible. By creating well-defined slot groups and using reward factors wisely, you'll help XO Scheduler's optimizer produce even better, more realistic schedules. Next, review your simulators and assign your new Time Slots to make them ready for scheduling.

articles.title: 🏷 Manage Properties – Creating and Managing Properties
articles.excerpt: How to create, configure, and manage properties in XO Scheduler.
articles.html:
🌟 In XO Scheduler, Properties are the backbone of your scheduling data. They're the attributes that describe and differentiate your resources, events, and other objects—making it possible to create accurate, conflict-free, and profitable schedules.

Think of properties as “labels” or “fields” you define to capture essential details, such as: an instructor's ID number, license expiry, or contact information; a simulator's cost or location; a classroom's available equipment; a trainee's ID number, date of birth.

By defining and customizing properties, you can control exactly what information is stored in your system, ensure consistency, and simplify scheduling automation.

🎥 Watch this 3-minute tutorial to see how to create a property, set it as unique or required, and activate it for the right resource types.

🧩 Key Concepts

Objects: everything in XO Scheduler—resources, events, classes, curriculums—can have properties. Resource Types: resources are grouped into types (e.g., Instructor, Simulator, Classroom); this grouping ensures properties are only applied where they make sense. System vs. Custom Properties: some properties (like Name, ID) are built-in, others you create yourself. Unique: a property marked as unique cannot have duplicate values across objects. Required: a required property must be filled in when adding a new resource or object.

🛠️ Step-by-Step: Creating and Managing Properties

1) Open the Properties Page — In XO Scheduler, go to Settings → Properties. Select the Object type you want to add the property to (e.g., Resources).

2) Create a New Property — Click Create Property on the right side window with a right mouse click. Give your property a Name (e.g., "Phone Number"). Choose the Data Type. Tip: even though it's a phone number, choose Text, so you can include international prefixes like +1 or +49.

3) Set Property Rules — Decide if it should be Unique (example: a phone number should be unique so two users can't share it). Decide if it should be Required (helps prevent missing data during setup).

4) Activate for Relevant Resource Types — Choose which resource types should have this property: ✅ Administrators, Instructors, Trainees; ❌ Classrooms, Fixed Devices, Simulators. Toggle each type On/Off as needed.

5) Save and Review — Click Save. Your new property now appears in the property list. Repeat this process for other fields you want to capture.

🔍 Example: Phone Number Property

In the video, we create a Phone Number property, set it to Text, make it Unique and Required, and activate it only for human resources (Administrators, Instructors, Trainees). This ensures irrelevant resources (like devices) aren't cluttered with unnecessary fields.

💡 Pro Tips

Plan properties in advance: list the key data points that truly matter for scheduling optimization. Keep it lean: too many properties make forms long and slow. Use system properties: built-in fields like Name and ID are always available—no need to recreate them. Deactivate instead of deleting: if a property becomes obsolete, deactivating keeps historical data intact.

🔗 What's Next?

Now that you know how to create a single property, let's explore Property Sets—collections of property values that make assigning attributes faster and more consistent.

articles.title: 🧩 Property Sets – Creating and Managing Property Sets
articles.excerpt: Understanding and Managing Property Sets in XO Scheduler
articles.html:
🌟 As your aviation training organization grows, so does the complexity of your data. That's where Property Sets come in.

A Property Set is a predefined collection of values for a property. Instead of letting users type values freely (which leads to typos, inconsistencies, and search headaches), a property set offers a clean drop-down menu of predefined options.

Example use cases: categorizing curriculums (Flight, Cabin, Dispatch, Maintenance); defining the fleet (A320, B777, B787); tagging training locations (London, Abu Dhabi, Bogota).

🎥 Video Tutorial: Creating and Using Property Sets — this 4-min tutorial shows how to create a property set, link it to a property, and use it when creating for example curriculums.

🧩 Why Use Property Sets?

Consistency: users select values instead of typing, avoiding mistakes like "Maintanance" vs. "Maintenance." Searchability: standardized data makes searching, filtering, and reporting seamless. Scalability: large organizations with thousands of resources and curriculums can organize data logically. Flexibility: add or edit values later without breaking historical data.

🛠️ Step-by-Step: Creating and Applying a Property Set

Below is a step-by-step guide using the example of creating a Training Type property set for curriculums (like in the video).

1) Create the Set — Navigate to Settings → Sets. Right-click on the set list to Create a New Set. Give your set a Name (e.g., Training Type). Add Set Elements by clicking ➕ — examples: Flight, Cabin, Dispatch, Maintenance. Click Save.

2) Create a Property Linked to the Set — Go to Settings → Properties. Select the Object type that will use this property (e.g., Curriculum). Right-click and choose Create Property. Give it the same name (e.g., Training Type). Under Property Type, select Set instead of Text. From the Set list, choose your newly created Training Type set. Mark it as Required (to ensure all curriculums have this property filled). Mark it as not Unique (multiple curriculums can share the same category). Save the property.

3) Apply the Property to Objects — Go to the Curriculums page. Create or edit a curriculum. You'll now see Training Type as a drop-down menu. Select one of your predefined values (e.g., Flight).

→ Enjoy the Benefits: when creating or editing curriculums, users no longer manually type categories. This ensures clean data entry and makes filtering or searching for curriculums by type effortless.

🔍 Example Recap

In the video, we created a Training Type Set with four options, linked that set to a new Training Type property, made it Required so every curriculum is categorized, and saw it in action — users can only select from the predefined values.

💡 Pro Tips

Keep sets tidy: if you have too many options, consider breaking them into multiple sets. Review periodically: outdated categories? Deactivate them rather than delete, preserving historical records. Use sets for reporting: standardized data makes filtering and analytics far more powerful. Start small: identify the 3–5 key properties that benefit most from sets, then expand.

articles.title: ⏱ Scheduling – Run the XO Optimizer
articles.excerpt: Learn how to create classes and run XO's Scheduler to generate fast, optimal training schedules.
articles.html:
Scheduling is the heart of XO Scheduler. Once your resources, curriculums, and qualifications are ready, the Optimizer can generate reliable schedules with just a few clicks.

This article will guide you through:

  • Creating one or multiple classes

  • - Configuring scheduling options

  • - Running the XO Scheduler for optimal results

✅ Before you start: Make sure you've completed all tutorials under "Get Ready and Prepare to Schedule." These steps—such as creating curriculums, qualifying resources, and setting work rules—are essential for accurate scheduling.

🛠️ Step-by-Step Guide

📸 Disclaimer: Screenshots and videos may look slightly different from your XO Scheduler interface depending on your version or configuration.

We'll use creating and scheduling a B777 December class as our example.

1) Create a class

In the bottom-left corner, right-click → Create Class.

A new window opens—fill in these fields:

  • Underlying Curriculum → Select which curriculum to base the class on.

  • - Start-Period Start / End → Define the time range when the class can begin.

  • - Class Name → e.g., B777 Dec.

  • - Location → Choose where the class takes place.

  • - Revenue → Enter revenue details for this class.

  • - Allowed Initial Week Day → Choose allowed start days (grey = allowed).

  • - Allowed Training Week Days → Choose training days (grey = allowed).

2) Choose class creation options

Under Create Multiple Classes, you have three choices:

  • Only one with the specific start-period → Create one class; XO finds the best start day.

  • - Create [ ] classes with start-period evenly distributed → Enter how many classes you want within the date range.

  • - Create classes with specific dates as start-period → Manually define exact start dates.

In this example we are creating 3 classes. Click Save. Your class(es) will now appear in the Classes window on the bottom-left.

3) Run scheduling

Select one or more classes from the Classes window (you can also choose "Select all" if needed). In this case we selected 2 out of the 3 classes we just created.

Right-click → Schedule.

The Schedule Configurator opens.

4) Select resources to schedule

Choose which resources XO should schedule:

  • Instructor

  • - Classroom

  • - Simulator

You can choose one, multiple, or all at once.

✅ For a full plan, click Complete so the system optimizes all resources simultaneously.

5) Run the optimizer

Click Run Scheduling. XO Scheduler finds the optimal solution. When finished, click Close.

6) Review the results

You'll see a "Complete" status next to the class. A colored horizontal bar on the right shows your scheduled days.

🎉 Your class is now fully scheduled!

💡 Pro Tips

  • Prepare first: Incomplete qualifications or missing work rules can cause scheduling errors.

  • - Use even distribution for multiple classes: Helps spread start dates for resource availability.

  • - Check allowed days: Limiting start or training days can affect optimizer flexibility.

  • - Visual confirmation: Use the colored Gantt bar to quickly verify scheduled days.

🔗 Related Tutorials

  • Create a Curriculum – Overview – Build the curriculums your classes will use

  • - Qualify Resources – Assign qualifications so instructors, simulators, and classrooms can be scheduled

  • - Work Rules – Set up work and rest rules for human resources

📌 Wrapping Up

The XO Optimizer makes scheduling fast and accurate. By defining classes, selecting resources, and running the scheduler, you ensure your training plans are both optimized and realistic.

Next, review your scheduled classes to confirm everything looks correct—or move on to managing changes and updates as your training schedule evolves.

articles.title: 🧠 Scheduling 2 – Optimizing Instructor Assignments with XO Scheduler
articles.excerpt: See how XO's global optimizer assigns instructors more efficiently than class-by-class scheduling.
articles.html:
💡 Introduction

Welcome to the second part of our Scheduling Series. In the first tutorial, you learned how to create classes and prepare them for scheduling. Now, we'll go a step further — behind the scenes of the optimizer itself.

In this session, you'll see how global mathematical optimization outperforms simple step-by-step or class-by-class scheduling methods.

You'll also watch the optimizer assign instructors efficiently across dozens of training classes, reducing workload fragmentation and maximizing profit.

📸 Disclaimer: Screenshots or video examples may differ slightly from your XO Scheduler interface, depending on your configuration.

🎥 Watch the Video:

This tutorial corresponds to the second video in the Scheduling Series. You'll learn the key principles of mathematical optimization, see how XO Scheduler builds optimal instructor assignments in real time, and compare global vs. class-by-class results.

  1. Understand the Concept of Optimization

  2. Traditional scheduling often follows a sequential or heuristic process — assigning one class or instructor at a time. This can lead to conflicts, inefficiencies, and partially filled schedules.

XO Scheduler uses a global optimizer, which evaluates all classes and all resources together to find the best overall solution — in seconds.

Let's look at a simple illustration (Resource → Lesson → Reward Example):

  • Resource 2 → Lesson 1 → $500

  • - Resource 1 → Lesson 2 → $850

  • - Resource 3 → Lesson 1 → $900

If we schedule lesson by lesson, we might quickly pick high-reward matches — but run out of qualified resources for the last lesson.

A global optimizer, instead, evaluates all combinations to achieve the highest total reward and complete utilization of resources.

This principle scales up to hundreds of instructors, simulators, and classes.

  1. Run the Optimizer in XO Scheduler

  2. Open your Scheduling Page.

  3. Select the classes to be scheduled — for example, your B747 Recurrent Training.

  4. Right-click → Schedule.

  5. In the Schedule Configurator, choose Instructors (since simulators and classrooms were already scheduled earlier).

  6. Click Run Schedule.

  1. Observe the Optimization Process

  2. The optimizer begins collecting data and building the model from zero.

  3. Progress is displayed at the top (e.g., 9% complete).

  4. It first focuses on continuity preferences, then moves toward maximizing total reward.

  5. You'll see in real time how the system assigns instructors and consolidates their workload.

  6. Example: 425 instructors assigned → 505 → 547 → all 550 slots filled

  7. Then, the optimizer enters the "less fragmented" phase, aiming to use fewer instructors more efficiently: 17 → 16 → 15 → 14 instructors total

  8. You can stop the process at any time if you're satisfied with the current solution.

  1. Analyze the Results

  2. - Total Profit: ≈ $347,000

  3. - Instructors Used: 14

  4. - All slots filled

  5. - Higher efficiency and better resource utilization

  1. Compare Global vs Class-by-Class Scheduling

  2. To illustrate the power of optimization (Scheduling Method → Instructors Used → Profit → Missing Assignments):

  3. - Global Optimizer → 14 → $347,000 → None

  4. - Class-by-Class → 15 → $340,000 → 4 classes incomplete

When scheduling class by class, the system locks each class once completed — preventing global rebalancing later. As a result, some slots remain unfilled even though additional instructors are available.

That's why global optimization is essential to achieve the best possible outcome.

💡 Pro Tip

Use the global optimizer whenever possible. It not only improves overall profit but also guarantees that every class gets a complete and feasible schedule.

🔗 Related Tutorials

  • 🎯 Scheduling 1 – Creating and Understanding Classes

  • - ⚙️ Work Rules – Define Duty and Rest Times

  • - 🧩 Curriculum Series – Building Your Training Structure

📘 Wrapping Up

The optimizer is what makes XO Scheduler stand out — transforming complex, multi-resource planning into a fast, transparent, and efficient process.

In the next tutorial, we'll explore how to review, adjust, and analyze scheduled results — refining your plan even further.

✅ Next Step

Continue to Scheduling 3 – Review and Adjust Schedules.

articles.title: 🚑 Handling a Sick Instructor – Reassigning a Class
articles.excerpt: Learn how to handle last-minute instructor absences by marking instructors unavailable, removing affected assignments, and re-scheduling classes — either automatically or manually.
articles.html:
In real-world training operations, schedules rarely stay perfect for long. Short-term disruptions are part of daily life — an instructor may call in sick, a simulator may go down for maintenance, or a classroom might suddenly become unavailable.

What matters most is how quickly and safely you can react — without breaking qualification requirements, workload limits, or training continuity.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how XO Scheduler helps you manage these daily changes:

  • by automatically finding a qualified replacement when possible, and

  • - by supporting manual intervention when capacity is tight.

📸 Disclaimer: Screenshots and videos may look slightly different from your XO Scheduler interface depending on your configuration.

🎥 Watch the Video

This tutorial includes a video walkthrough showing how to handle instructor sick leave in different scenarios — including automatic replacement and manual reassignment when no capacity is available.

🧭 Step-by-Step Guide

We'll use two realistic examples: a case where a replacement is available, and a case where manual intervention is required.

1) Locate the Affected Class

In the bottom-left Classes section, locate the affected class.

Click the small arrow next to the class name to expand the days.

Select the affected day to reveal its topics and events.

2) Remove the Sick Instructor from Assigned Events

In the bottom-right Events section, double-click an event where the instructor is assigned (for example, Briefing or Human Factors).

In the event window, go to Resources.

Find the instructor's name and click the trash icon to remove them.

Click Save.

In our example, we are removing Emily Parker from the event. Repeat this step for all affected events.

You'll now see the class marked as "Partially Scheduled", indicating an instructor is missing.

3) Mark the Instructor as Unavailable (Sick Leave)

Before we let the XO System run the Scheduling again to find another instructor, we have to make sure to mark the instructor as unavailable — otherwise the optimizer may assign them again.

In the top-right Resources section, select the instructor and the affected day.

Right-click → Create Event.

In the new event window:

  • Name: e.g., Sick Leave.

  • - Dates & Time: Specify the exact day and time (XO uses a 24/7 schedule; end-of-day is 11:59 PM).

  • - Location: Choose the correct location.

  • - Color: Pick a distinct color for sick leave.

  • - Counts for Workload: Set according to your company's policy. Some organizations count sick leave toward workload, while others do not. Choose Yes or No based on your rules.

  • Click Save.

4) Re-run Scheduling to Find a Replacement

Return to the affected class.

Right-click on the class → Schedule.

In the scheduling window, select Instructor as the resource to schedule.

Click Run Scheduling.

The Optimizer will search for a qualified instructor who is available and assign them to the class.

5) Automatic Replacement (When Capacity Is Available)

If a qualified and available instructor exists:

  • The optimizer will automatically assign a substitute.

  • - All qualifications, work rules, rest times, and continuity rules are respected.

  • - The class status returns to "Complete".

6) Manual Assignment (When No Replacement Is Found)

In high-utilization scenarios (for example, heavily loaded fleets), the optimizer may not find a replacement. In this case:

  • Filter the Resources list for external or third-party instructors.

  • - Select a qualified instructor manually.

  • - Assign them directly to the affected events.

  • This allows you to resolve last-minute issues even when internal capacity is exhausted.

7) Verify the Final Result

  • Confirm the class is marked as Complete

  • - Review the Gantt chart and event details

  • - Ensure all assignments respect qualifications and work rules

💡 Pro Tips

  • Always mark sick leave first: Otherwise, the optimizer may reassign the same instructor

  • - Use presets: Consistent presets for sick leave improve speed and clarity

  • - Check workload rules: Especially when assigning substitutes manually

  • - Plan for peak periods: External instructors can be critical during high-load phases

🔗 Related Tutorials

  • Scheduling – Run the XO Optimizer – Learn how to schedule and re-schedule classes

  • - Qualify Resources – Ensure instructors have the right qualifications for substitution

  • - Work Rules – Make sure duty limits are considered for replacements

  • - How to Manage Daily Events and Presets

📌 Wrapping Up

Last-minute changes like sick calls are part of everyday training operations. By marking instructors unavailable and using XO Scheduler's optimizer — with manual fallback when needed — you can keep training running smoothly, safely, and efficiently.

This is exactly what the Dailies workflows are designed for: handling the unexpected without losing control.

articles.title: 🗂 How to Manage Daily Events and Presets
articles.excerpt: Learn how to manually create, edit, and organize events such as simulator maintenance, instructor vacations, or sick leave — and how to simplify your work using presets.
articles.html:
💡 Introduction

Not all activities in XO Scheduler are planned automatically. Some events — like simulator maintenance, vacations, or office work — need to be entered manually so the system can respect them when scheduling.

To make this process faster and more consistent, XO Scheduler uses Presets, which act as templates with predefined values such as color, name, or workload settings.

This tutorial shows you how to:

  • Create manual events directly in the Gantt view

  • - Use existing presets for quick setup

  • - Create your own new presets for future use

📸 Disclaimer: Screenshots or video examples may look slightly different from your version of XO Scheduler, depending on your organization's configuration.

🎥 Watch the video:

Below you'll find a quick video walkthrough showing exactly how to create and manage events and presets in XO Scheduler.

🧭 Step-by-Step Guide

We'll go through three practical examples: Simulator maintenance, Instructor office work, and Sick leave.

  1. Create a Maintenance Event for a Simulator

  2. In the main Gantt view, locate the simulator you want to block.

  3. Right-click on the desired date → select Create Event.

  4. In the event window, select the preset Sim Maintenance (if available). This automatically fills in the name, color, and location.

  5. ⚠️ Note: If the preset doesn't already exist, you'll need to create it first — go to Number 3 of this tutorial.

  6. Define the end date (e.g., 10th March).

  7. Click Save.

  8. The maintenance event now appears in the Gantt chart. When you next run the optimizer, XO Scheduler will treat this time as unavailable for that simulator.

  1. Create an Office Work Event for an Instructor

  2. Find the instructor in the Gantt view.

  3. Right-click → Create Event.

  4. Choose the preset Office Work.

  5. ⚠️ Note: If the preset doesn't already exist, you'll need to create it first — go to Number 3 of this tutorial.

  6. Set the date and time, for example: Start: 4th March, 08:00. End: 4th March, 18:00.

  7. Enable Counts for Workload = Yes (if office work should count toward working hours).

  8. To make it repeat daily, activate Repeat → Daily until 11th March.

  9. Click Save.

  10. This event will be visible in the Gantt chart, and the scheduler will include it in workload balancing.

  1. Create a Sick Leave Preset and Event

  2. If the preset doesn't already exist, you'll need to create it first.

Step 3.1: Create the Preset

Go to Setup → Properties.

Go to "Manage Properties for: Events" and click Manage Properties.

Under Manage Presets, right-click → Create Custom Preset.

Name it Sick Leave.

Set:

  • Color (for easy visibility on the Gantt)

  • - Counts for Workload = No

  • - Location = empty, so it inherits the resource's location

  • Click Save.

Step 3.2: Create a Sick Leave for an Instructor

Go to the Gantt view.

Select the instructor → Right-click → Create Event.

Choose your new Sick Leave preset.

Define the start and end dates (e.g., 4th–6th March).

Click Save.

The instructor's schedule now correctly reflects the absence, and the optimizer will not assign any sessions during this period.

💡 Pro Tip

Use presets to ensure consistency in naming, color coding, and workload rules. They're especially helpful when your organization has many recurring event types — like vacation, training leave, or technical downtime.

If your company setup differs, you might see additional optional fields. Just fill out what's relevant to you.

🔗 Related Tutorials

  • 🩺 Handling a Sick Instructor - without a Preset

  • - ✈ Work Rules: Define Duty and Rest Times

  • - ⚙️ Managing Properties

📘 Wrapping Up

Using Events and Presets keeps your schedule clean and organized — and ensures the optimizer respects real-world constraints like absences or maintenance.

This small effort in setup saves major headaches later — helping your scheduling stay accurate and realistic day by day.

A Property Set is a predefined collection of values for a property. Instead of letting users type values freely (which leads to typos, inconsistencies, and search headaches), a property set offers a clean drop-down menu of predefined options.

Example use cases:

  • Categorizing curriculums (Flight, Cabin, Dispatch, Maintenance)

  • - Defining the fleet (A320, B777, B787)

  • - Tagging training locations (London, Abu Dhabi, Bogota)

🎥 Video Tutorial: Creating and Using Property Sets

This 4-min tutorial shows how to create a property set, link it to a property, and use it when creating for example curriculums.

📸 Disclaimer: Screenshots and videos may look slightly different from your XO Scheduler interface depending on your version or configuration.

🧩 Why Use Property Sets?

  • Consistency: Users select values instead of typing, avoiding mistakes like "Maintanance" vs. "Maintenance."

  • - Searchability: Standardized data makes searching, filtering, and reporting seamless.

  • - Scalability: Large organizations with thousands of resources and curriculums can organize data logically.

  • - Flexibility: Add or edit values later without breaking historical data.

🛠️ Step-by-Step: Creating and Applying a Property Set

Below is a step-by-step guide using the example of creating a Training Type property set for curriculums (like in the video). There are of course many other examples, but this one will help you clearly understand how to work with property sets.

1) Create the Set

Navigate to Settings → Sets.

Right-click on the set list to Create a New Set.

Give your set a Name (e.g., Training Type).

Add Set Elements by clicking ➕. Examples: Flight, Cabin, Dispatch, Maintenance.

Click Save.

2) Create a Property Linked to the Set

Go to Settings → Properties.

Select the Object type that will use this property (e.g., Curriculum).

Right-click and choose Create Property.

Give it the same name (e.g., Training Type).

Under Property Type, select Set instead of Text.

From the Set list, choose your newly created Training Type set.

Mark it as Required (to ensure all curriculums have this property filled).

Mark it as not Unique (multiple curriculums can share the same category).

Save the property.

3) Apply the Property to Objects

Go to the Curriculums page.

Create or edit a curriculum.

You'll now see Training Type as a drop-down menu.

Select one of your predefined values (e.g., Flight).

→ Enjoy the Benefits: When creating or editing curriculums, users no longer manually type categories. This ensures clean data entry and makes filtering or searching for curriculums by type effortless.

🔍 Example Recap

In the video, we:

  • Created a Training Type Set with four options.

  • - Linked that set to a new Training Type property.

  • - Made it Required so every curriculum is categorized.

  • - Saw it in action—users can only select from the predefined values.

💡 Pro Tips

  • Keep sets tidy: If you have too many options, consider breaking them into multiple sets.

  • - Review periodically: Outdated categories? Deactivate them rather than delete, preserving historical records.

  • - Use sets for reporting: Standardized data makes filtering and analytics far more powerful.

  • - Start small: Identify the 3–5 key properties that benefit most from sets, then expand.
